# marmot_task (Resource)

~> **Requires Marmot Cloud or Marmot Enterprise.** Open-source Marmot has no Tasks API, and an instance where Tasks is not enabled refuses every request, so this resource fails on apply there.

A Marmot Task: a goal written as a prompt, which an agent completes in the background whenever the `trigger` fires. The agent can search the catalog, read assets and run governed, read-only queries, and nothing else.

A task has no access of its own. It runs as the principal that last saved it: the one behind the provider's credential, or the service account named in `run_as_service_account_id`. Every apply that changes the task makes it run as that principal again, whoever saved it before; `run_as` reports who that is.

A `once` trigger without `run_at` runs the task one time, when it is created. Changing the task afterwards does not run it again.

See the [Tasks guide](../guides/tasks.md) for who a task runs as and what it can reach.

## Report on a schedule

```terraform
resource "marmot_task" "weekly_revenue" {
  name        = "weekly-revenue"
  description = "Monday revenue digest for the finance team"
  prompt      = "Report last week's revenue by region and compare it with the week before."

  trigger = {
    type = "schedule"
    cron = "0 8 * * 1"
  }

  sources = ["warehouse"]
}
```

## Run as a service account

Without `run_as_service_account_id` the task runs as the principal behind the provider's credential. Naming an account keeps the task's access separate from the access of whoever applies the configuration.

```terraform
resource "marmot_service_account" "revenue_reporter" {
  name        = "revenue-reporter"
  description = "Runs the weekly revenue task. Owned by the finance team."
}

resource "marmot_task" "weekly_revenue" {
  name   = "weekly-revenue"
  prompt = "Report last week's revenue by region and compare it with the week before."

  trigger = {
    type = "schedule"
    cron = "0 8 * * 1"
  }

  run_as_service_account_id = marmot_service_account.revenue_reporter.id
}
```

## React to catalog events

```terraform
resource "marmot_task" "schema_watch" {
  name   = "schema-watch"
  prompt = "Describe what changed in the schema and which downstream assets it may break."

  trigger = {
    type   = "event"
    events = ["asset.schema_changed"]

    filter = {
      asset_types = ["table"]
      providers   = ["bigquery"]
    }

    cooldown_seconds = 900
  }
}
```

## Run once

A `once` trigger without `run_at` runs the task one time, when the resource is created. Changing the prompt or anything else afterwards updates the task and does not run it again. To run it again, replace the resource:

```shell
terraform apply -replace=marmot_task.orphaned_tables
```

```terraform
# Runs one time, as soon as it is created.
resource "marmot_task" "orphaned_tables" {
  name   = "orphaned-tables"
  prompt = "List the tables without an owner, largest first."

  trigger = {
    type = "once"
  }
}

# Runs one time, at the given moment.
resource "marmot_task" "year_end_summary" {
  name   = "year-end-summary"
  prompt = "Summarise this year's revenue by quarter."

  trigger = {
    type   = "once"
    run_at = "2026-12-31T17:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

## Cap a run

```terraform
resource "marmot_task" "weekly_revenue" {
  name   = "weekly-revenue"
  prompt = "Report last week's revenue by region and compare it with the week before."

  trigger = {
    type = "schedule"
    cron = "0 8 * * 1"
  }

  # What is left out takes the instance default.
  limits = {
    max_queries     = 5
    timeout_seconds = 300
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the task, unique per instance.
- `prompt` (String) The goal the agent works towards, in plain language, up to 8000 characters.
- `trigger` (Attributes) When the task runs. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--trigger))

### Optional

- `description` (String) What the task is for.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the task runs when its trigger fires. Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to keep the task but pause it.
- `limits` (Attributes) Caps on a single run. The server fills in the instance default for each limit left out, and the instance sets a ceiling for each. A limit taken out of the configuration keeps its value until the task next changes, and then goes back to the instance default. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--limits))
- `run_as_service_account_id` (String) ID of a `marmot_service_account` to run the task as, instead of the principal behind the provider's credential. Naming one requires the `serviceAccount:manage` permission on the organization. The task can reach what that account can, and nothing more.
- `sources` (Set of String) Queryable sources the agent may query, for example `warehouse`. This only narrows what `run_as` may query. Omit to allow every source `run_as` may query.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp
- `id` (String) Task ID
- `run_as` (Attributes) The principal the task runs as: whoever last saved it, or the service account named in `run_as_service_account_id`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--run_as))
- `updated_at` (String) Last update timestamp

<a id="nestedatt--trigger"></a>
### Nested Schema for `trigger`

Required:

- `type` (String) `once` runs the task a single time, `schedule` on a cron, `event` when the catalog changes.

Optional:

- `cooldown_seconds` (Number) Cooldown of an `event` task in seconds, from 60 to 86400. Events are debounced and folded into at most one pending run. Omit to leave the cooldown to the server.
- `cron` (String) Five-field cron expression of a `schedule` task, in UTC, for example `0 8 * * 1`. Required for `schedule`.
- `events` (Set of String) Catalog events that run an `event` task: `asset.created`, `asset.updated`, `asset.schema_changed`, `asset.deleted`, `lineage.changed`, `ingestion.completed`, `ingestion.failed`. Required for `event`.
- `filter` (Attributes) Narrows the events that run an `event` task. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--trigger--filter))
- `run_at` (String) When a `once` task runs, as an RFC 3339 timestamp such as `2026-12-01T08:00:00Z`. Omit to run it when it is created. The server answers in UTC; a timestamp with another offset naming the same instant is kept as written.

<a id="nestedatt--trigger--filter"></a>
### Nested Schema for `trigger.filter`

Optional:

- `asset_types` (Set of String) Asset types to match, for example `table`.
- `pipelines` (Set of String) Pipelines to match.
- `providers` (Set of String) Asset providers to match, for example `bigquery`.



<a id="nestedatt--limits"></a>
### Nested Schema for `limits`

Optional:

- `max_queries` (Number) Queries the agent may run.
- `max_rows` (Number) Rows per query.
- `max_steps` (Number) Steps the agent may take.
- `max_tokens` (Number) Model tokens the run may use.
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Wall-clock time the run may take, in seconds.


<a id="nestedatt--run_as"></a>
### Nested Schema for `run_as`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) ID of the principal.
- `name` (String) Name of the principal.
- `type` (String) `user` or `service_account`.

## Import

Tasks are imported by their ID:

```shell
terraform import marmot_task.weekly_revenue 018e1234-5678-7abc-def0-123456789abc
```

The server reports who a task runs as, not whether a request named that service account. After an import `run_as_service_account_id` is absent from state, so a configuration that sets it shows it as an addition in the first plan. Applying that sends the task again, which makes it run as the account it names.
